top_story: Syria’s 24 April arrest of former regime official Amjad Youssef, accused of leading the 2013 Tadamon massacre, marks a rare move toward accountability that could test how far Damascus is willing to revisit wartime atrocities beyond symbolic cases. Two days earlier in Lebanon, the apparent Israeli targeting of journalist Amal Khalil underscored how the regional conflict environment continues to erase civilian protections and deepen fear among media workers and communities already living under persistent threat. These developments follow a month of heightened US-Iran confrontation, after Trump’s 23 March threat against Iran’s power grid drew vows of regional retaliation from Tehran and reinforced a climate in which coercive signaling by states translates into sharper risks for civilians across neighboring fronts. The emerging picture is of a region where justice remains selective, deterrence is increasingly violent, and noncombatants bear the most immediate cost.
